quarterly_data.signal: Fluor 10-K: 2025 revenue was $15,503 million (2024: $16,315 million) - Urban Solutions $9,200 million (2024: $7,239 million), Energy Solutions $3,554 million ($5,976 million), Mission Solutions $2,720 million ($2,594 million). Total segment result was a loss of $109 million (2024: profit of $635 million, 3.9% margin): Urban Solutions profit $205 million (2.2% margin), Energy Solutions a loss of $414 million, Mission Solutions profit $94 million (3.5% margin). Net loss attributable to Fluor was $51 million (2024: net earnings of $2,145 million).
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $15,503 million (2024: $16,315 million); segment loss of $109 million

quarterly_data.signal: Fluor 10-K: Energy Solutions segment profit declined in 2025 due to the reversal of previously recognized revenue of $643 million (or $3.89 per share) for a judgment on the long completed Santos project in Australia. Urban Solutions segment profit decreased on forecast adjustments of $108 million (or $0.61 per share) for cost growth on 3 infrastructure projects (subcontracted design errors, price escalation, schedule impacts), partly offset by improved performance on other infrastructure projects, a favorable negotiation with a designer and the ramp up of life sciences projects.
quarterly_data.figure: $643 million revenue reversal (Santos judgment); $108 million infrastructure forecast adjustments

quarterly_data.signal: Fluor 10-K: 2025 new awards were $11,956 million (2024: $15,123 million) - Urban Solutions $8,688 million, Energy Solutions $1,421 million, Mission Solutions $1,847 million; 26% related to projects outside the U.S. Urban Solutions awards included a large multi-billion dollar pharmaceutical facility, two significant mining projects and construction contracts for 2 infrastructure projects; Mission Solutions awards included a six-year contract to extend Fluor's presence at the Portsmouth site.

Fluor 10-K: backlog at December 31, 2025 was $25,536 million (December 31, 2024: $28,484 million) - Urban Solutions $18,746 million, Energy Solutions $4,601 million, Mission Solutions $2,189 million; 40% related to projects outside the U.S. and 81% to reimbursable projects. Backlog decreased because execution pace exceeded new award activity; Fluor expects to execute approximately half of its ending 2025 backlog in 2026. Mission Solutions backlog included $1.0 billion of unfunded government contracts (2024: $665 million).

Fluor 10-K: backlog at December 31, 2025 included $255 million for legacy projects in a loss position (2024: $702 million), including approximately $212 million of estimated unfunded losses (2024: $237 million).
quarterly_data.figure: $255 million legacy loss-project backlog; approximately $212 million unfunded losses

quarterly_data.signal: Fluor 10-K: 2025 operating cash flow was negative $387 million (2024: $828 million); capital expenditures were $50 million (2024: $164 million), primarily investments in IT; cash and cash equivalents were $2,135 million at year-end 2025. In 2025 Fluor completed the sale of Stork's operations in the U.K.

Fluor 10-K: its advanced technologies and manufacturing business delivers front-end engineering, program management and EPC services across market segments including data centers and semiconductors; Fluor's stated strategy is to grow its market positions in energy addition, low carbon power, LNG, sustainable chemicals, data centers, semiconductors, critical metals and minerals and national security. Its national security business also provides the intelligence community with data center management and operations and maintenance of secure facilities.
